record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Optimality of Algorithm 7.2 for regular sequences
record.original_question: For the single-machine problem with processing times p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t and objective sum_j C_j, let beta_j = 1 + b_j be the deterioration-rate factor sequence. Suppose this sequence is regular, such as an arithmetic sequence, geometric sequence, or Fibonacci sequence. Algorithm 7.2 constructs a V-shaped schedule in O(n) time by using the periodic sign behavior of the signature S^-(beta), rather than recomputing that signature during the greedy construction. Does Algorithm 7.2 always generate an optimal schedule for every regular sequence of deterioration-rate factors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the single-machine scheduling problem with n jobs whose processing times depend on their starting times in the linear deteriorating form
  p_j(t) = 1 + b_j · t,   j = 1, …, n,
where b_j > 0 and t ≥ 0 denotes the starting time of job j. All jobs are available at time 0 and the machine processes at most one job at a time without preemption. For a permutation π = (π(1), …, π(n)) the completion times are defined recursively by C_{π(0)} = 0 and C_{π(k)} = (1 + b_{π(k)}) · (1 + C_{π(k−1)}). The objective is to minimize the total completion time Σ_{j=1}^n C_j.

Define the deterioration-rate factors β_j = 1 + b_j and let β = (β_1, …, β_n) be a fixed sequence. For a permutation, the signature S^−(β) records the sign pattern of certain pairwise comparisons used to determine when swapping adjacent jobs decreases the objective; this signature is known to exhibit periodic behavior when the sequence β is "regular," for instance when (β_j) is an arithmetic progression, a geometric progression, or a Fibonacci-type sequence.

Algorithm 7.2 is a greedy procedure that, exploiting this periodic sign behavior of S^−(β) instead of recomputing it during construction, builds a V-shaped schedule (i.e. a schedule whose β-values are non-increasing up to a minimum and non-decreasing thereafter) in O(n) time.

Question: Does Algorithm 7.2 produce a schedule that minimizes Σ_j C_j for every regular sequence β of deterioration-rate factors (in particular, for every arithmetic, geometric, or Fibonacci sequence)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture in the survey on time-dependent scheduling. Subsequent literature on V-shaped optimal sequencing for single-machine deteriorating-job problems (e.g., refined optimality conditions and notes on exact algorithms/heuristics for V- and Λ-shaped sequences) addresses related properties but does not appear to confirm or refute the optimality of the specific O(n) greedy procedure for all regular β-sequences. No resolution of the conjecture was located.
